The '''2026 Sefton Metropolitan Borough Council election''' is scheduled to be held on Thursday 7 May 2026, alongside [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections in the United Kingdom]]. The whole Council of 66 members of [[Sefton Metropolitan Borough Council]] in [[Merseyside]] will be elected.

Labour retained control of the council on a significantly reduced majority, while the Liberal Democrats nearly doubled their number of councillors. Reform UK won its first councillors at an election in the borough, while the Greens enjoyed their best result to this point in terms of both seats and vote share. Lydiate and Maghull Community Independents won 5 seats, while the Conservatives lost all representation on the council.

On 12 May, a Reform UK councillor resigned within days of being elected.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hamilton |first=Claire |date=2026-05-12 |title=Reform councillor resigns over Holocaust 'hoax' post |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c1j2wexpy03o |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=[[BBC News]] |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Background==
Sefton Metropolitan Borough Council was created in 1974. The [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] controlled the council from its creation until [[1984 Sefton Metropolitan Borough Council election|1986]], when the council fell into [[no overall control]].<ref>{{cite web |title=BBC News - Election 2011 - England council elections - Sefton |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/special/election2011/council/html/ca.stm |website=BBC News |access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref> [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] became the largest party in [[1988 Sefton Metropolitan Borough Council election|1988]] but did not form their first majority administration until [[2012 Sefton Metropolitan Borough Council election|24 years later]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sefton Council Election Results 1973-2012 |url=https://www.electionscentre.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/Sefton-1973-2012.pdf |website=Elections Centre |access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref> The [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] briefly became the largest party between [[2000 Sefton Metropolitan Borough Council election|2000]] and [[2002 Sefton Metropolitan Borough Council election|2002]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Vote 2002 - Sefton |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/hi/english/static/vote2002/local_elections/122.stm |access-date=9 January 2026 |work=BBC News}}</ref> and again for the more prolonged period between [[2004 Sefton Metropolitan Borough Council election|2004]] and [[2011 Sefton Metropolitan Borough Council election|2011]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hall |first1=Sarah |title=Best ever results just a start, says Kennedy |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2004/jun/12/uk.localgovernment6 |access-date=9 January 2026 |work=The Guardian |date=12 June 2004}}</ref> Labour have formed majority administrations since 2012 with the Liberal Democrats serving as the principal opposition (aside from [[2021 Sefton Metropolitan Borough Council election|2021]] which saw the Conservatives hold an equal number of seats).

In the [[2024 Sefton Metropolitan Borough Council election|most recent election]], Labour made no net gains or losses, winning a seat from the Conservatives but also losing a seat to the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] and giving the Greens their first seat on the council.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Haygarth |first1=Dan |last2=Barnes |first2=Edward |last3=Westwood |first3=Katie |last4=Jessett |first4=Elliot |last5=Thorp |first5=Liam |title=Sefton Council local elections 2024 result in full |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/sefton-council-local-elections-2024-29085070 |access-date=9 January 2026 |work=Liverpool Echo |date=2 May 2024 |language=en}}</ref> The Liberal Democrats also held a seat gained through a defection from the Conservatives.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rand |first1=Lisa |title=Former Sefton conservative councillor joins Liberal Democrats |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/former-sefton-conservative-councillor-delighted-26905075 |access-date=9 January 2026 |work=Liverpool Echo |date=12 May 2023 |language=en}}</ref>
